enforced_by: the copywriter, the video teardown, email production

rows.name: Intensification
rows.what: Keep generating fresh, concrete pictures of the desire already fulfilled — never the same picture twice; vary the angle so repetition reinforces instead of tiring.

rows.name: Identification
rows.what: Build a saleable personality into the product by attaching roles the audience wants to be seen playing. The product then does double duty: physical satisfaction plus a badge of identity.

rows.name: Gradualization
rows.what: Belief is structural, not only a matter of content. A claim's strength equals its own content plus how far the copy has already prepared the audience to accept it — so build a chain of acceptances from a fact already believed, each step earning the next.

rows.name: Redefinition
rows.what: Give the product, or the problem, a new definition that removes an objection before it is consciously raised.

rows.name: Mechanization
rows.what: Verbal proof of HOW the product delivers — reason-why copy answering the silent question of how the thing works.

rows.name: Concentration
rows.what: Destroy the alternate ways of satisfying the desire — a direct attack on the competing option or on the status quo.

rows.name: Camouflage
rows.what: Borrow believability from the medium the ad lives in. Editorial and organic content is trusted more than advertising voice, so minimise the gear change between the two.
